b386e728.text:
Feature: let an instruction step reference the recipe's notes.

A step can point at ingredients (its ingredient_references carry the ingredient's reference_id), but there is no way to attach one of the recipe's notes to a step. Users want the step view to show the note that belongs to it, so every note needs a stable identity and every step a list of note links.

Expected:
- Every recipe note gets a stable reference_id (UUID). RecipeNote (mealie.schema.recipe.recipe_notes) gains reference_id: UUID, generated (uuid4) when missing, null or empty; the API serializes it as referenceId, so recipe responses carry one more key per note while title and text are unchanged, and RecipeNote(...).model_dump(mode="json") must serialize it.
- A new NoteReference model in mealie.schema.recipe.recipe_step (exported from mealie.schema.recipe) with reference_id: UUID | None = None. RecipeStep gains note_references: list[NoteReference], default an empty list, next to ingredient_references.
- Data model: the notes table gets a nullable, indexed reference_id GUID column, generated for new rows and filled with a fresh UUID for every existing note when the migration runs. A new table recipe_note_ref_link stores the links: integer id primary key, instruction_id (GUID, foreign key to recipe_instructions.id, nullable, indexed), reference_id (GUID, nullable, indexed) and the base created_at/update_at timestamps (created_at indexed like the other base tables). RecipeInstruction gets a note_references relationship to it with delete-orphan cascade, built from the step's note_references the way ingredient_references are built, and excluded from its model config in the same way. Loading a recipe eager-loads the note references like the ingredient references.
- Round trip through the repositories: a recipe created with notes=[RecipeNote(title=..., text=...)] and recipe_instructions=[RecipeStep(text=..., note_references=[])] comes back with notes[0].reference_id set; after setting recipe_instructions[0].note_references = [NoteReference(reference_id=that id)] and calling repos.recipes.update(slug, recipe), the returned recipe's first step has exactly one note reference whose reference_id is that id.
- On a recipe update, note references whose note is no longer on the recipe are dropped from the steps, as is already done for ingredient references.
- Duplicating a recipe still copies the notes (title and text). The editor wiring is not graded.

b5c089f5.text:
Feature: standardized units, unit conversion, and merging shopping list items across convertible units.

List items only merge on the same unit id, so 2 cups and 1 pint never combine. Give each unit an optional standard expression (a quantity of a base unit), fill it in for known units, and merge list items with it. pint (>= 0.25, installed) converts; add it to the dependencies.

Expected:
1. IngredientUnitModel gets standard_quantity (Float, nullable) and standard_unit (String, nullable). CreateIngredientUnit (so the units API, JSON standardQuantity/standardUnit) gets both, default None; when standard_unit is empty or the quantity is not > 0, both become None. A StandardizedUnitType StrEnum (mealie.schema.recipe.recipe_ingredient, exported from mealie.schema.recipe): fluid_ounce, cup, ounce, pound, milliliter, liter, gram, kilogram.
2. The units repository standardizes on create and create_many when neither field is given: name, plural_name, abbreviation or plural_abbreviation (case-insensitive) is looked up in a map from every name/plural/abbreviation of the locale's seed units to the seed key, cached on the repository as `_standardized_unit_map` (a test sets it to {word: "gallon"}). Seed key to standard: teaspoon 1/6 and tablespoon 1/2 fluid_ounce, fluid-ounce 1 fluid_ounce, cup 1, pint 2, quart 4 and gallon 16 cup, milligram 1/1000 gram, and milliliter, liter, pound, ounce, gram, kilogram 1 of themselves. "gallon" in any of the four fields gives "cup" and 16; a random name gives None/None; user-supplied values are stored as given; an incomplete pair is cleared.
3. Seeding en-US still creates 24 units, "pint" standardized as 2 cup. The migration backfills existing units the same way against every locale's seed file, so restoring an older backup (a fixture is added to the restore test) leaves every group's "pint" at 2 cup.
4. mealie.services.parser_services.parser_utils exports UnitConverter, UnitNotFound (an Exception) and merge_quantity_and_unit, on pint unit names. parse(unit, strict=False) returns a pint.Unit (a pint.Unit passes through), an unknown string unchanged, or raises UnitNotFound when strict. can_convert(a, b): True for compatible units (strings or units) and for ounce against a volume (read as fluid ounce); False otherwise, unknown strings included. convert(q, unit, to_unit) and merge(q1, u1, q2, u2) return (float, pint.Unit), merge summing in the first unit, zero and negative quantities allowed (4 ounce + 1 cup = (12, "fluid_ounce")); an unknown unit raises UnitNotFound, incompatible units pint.errors.DimensionalityError. merge_quantity_and_unit(q1, unit1, q2, unit2) takes two unit models with standard data and returns (quantity, one of them): the sum in the larger unit when >= 1, else the smaller (1 pint-unit + 1 cup-unit -> (1.5, pint); 0.125 pint + 0.5 cup -> (0.75, cup)); an unknown standard_unit raises UnitNotFound, missing standard data ValueError.
5. Shopping list items merge across units when both carry convertible standard data: bulk-creating (POST /api/households/shopping/items/create-bulk) two items with the same note, unit A (1 cup) and unit B (2 cup), answers 201 with one createdItems entry, unitId B and quantity (qA + 2*qB) / 2. With different notes, or 1 cup against 2 gram, both items come back unchanged.

8d6783bc.text:
Feature: an optional duration on each recipe instruction step.

Users want to record how long a step takes ("rest 1 hour"), see it on the step and edit it in the recipe editor. Store it per step, in whole seconds. The editor and step view wiring is not graded.

Expected:
1. RecipeStep gets duration_seconds (durationSeconds in JSON): optional, default null, a whole number of seconds from 1 to 2147483647. Missing, null, 0 and 0.0 all mean no duration (None). Whole numbers in range are accepted, including JSON numbers written as floats with no fraction (1.0, 1e0, 2147483647.0); they are stored and returned as int. Anything else is a validation error: true and false, negatives (-1), fractions (0.5, 1.5, 2147483647.5), inf, -inf and nan, any string ("90", "0", "PT1M", "", " "), and values above 2147483647 (2147483648, 2147483648.0, 1e30). Nothing is rounded or read from a string. In RecipeStep.model_json_schema(by_alias=True), durationSeconds is not required, its default is null, and its anyOf has exactly two entries: an integer with minimum 1 and maximum 2147483647 (no other keywords), then null.
2. The RecipeInstruction ORM model gets a duration_seconds column on recipe_instructions: Integer, nullable, with no default and no server default. A RecipeInstruction built from a step's model_dump() keeps the exact seconds, and handle_one_to_many_list can set (42) and clear (None) it on an existing instruction without touching its text.
3. The migration only adds that column. Its offline SQL for sqlite and postgresql contains ALTER TABLE recipe_instructions ADD COLUMN duration_seconds INTEGER, with no NOT NULL, no DEFAULT and no UPDATE; existing rows get NULL. Its downgrade drops only that column and leaves every other table and row as it was: on a populated database, downgrading, upgrading, setting values, downgrading again and upgrading again must work repeatedly, and after an upgrade no row has a duration.
4. Through the API, PUT /api/recipes/{slug} stores each step's durationSeconds and GET returns it (null for a step sent without it or with null). A later PUT can change it, or clear it with null or 0, and the step keeps its text. An invalid value answers 422 and nothing is saved. The raw JSON export (TemplateService(...).render(recipe, "raw")) includes durationSeconds, and importing that JSON in a zip (POST /api/recipes/create/zip) restores it.

d340fdd9.text:
Fix: stored normalized text and search normalization disagree, so punctuation breaks search.

Search normalizes the query (SearchFilter._normalize_search with normalize_characters=True) by replacing punctuation with spaces, but the *_normalized columns written through SqlAlchemyBase.normalize only transliterate, lower-case and strip. "Gluten-Free Bread" is stored as "gluten-free bread" and searched as "gluten free bread", so the recipe is not found.

Expected:
- SqlAlchemyBase.normalize(val) (mealie.db.models._model_base) transliterates (unidecode), replaces every ASCII punctuation character except the apostrophe and the double quote with one space (no collapsing of the spaces), lower-cases, strips and caps at 255 characters: "Gluten-Free Bread" -> "gluten free bread", "Mac & Cheese" -> "mac   cheese" (three spaces), "Chicken/Rice Bowl" -> "chicken rice bowl", "Rátàtôuile" -> "ratatouile", "Mom's Pasta" -> "mom's pasta".
- SearchFilter._normalize_search(name, normalize_characters=True) returns the identical string for the same inputs; both sides share one definition of the punctuation set.
- A data migration re-normalizes the existing rows, reading each source column and rewriting its normalized column with the new rule: recipes (name -> name_normalized, description -> description_normalized), recipes_ingredients (note -> note_normalized, original_text -> original_text_normalized), ingredient_units (name, plural_name, abbreviation, plural_abbreviation and their _normalized columns), ingredient_foods (name, plural_name), ingredient_units_aliases (name) and ingredient_foods_aliases (name). NULL stays NULL. Restoring the fixture backups (the backup restore tests) must still work.

The accepted targets are only the three punctuation cases of each parametrized test; the accent and apostrophe cases already pass. The test_backup_v2.py change only removes an unused helper.

0254fd7d.text:
Fix: remove the dead rows left in the legacy cookbook and meal plan rule organizer join tables.

Cookbooks and meal plan rules used to be filtered by categories, tags and tools through join tables: cookbooks_to_categories, cookbooks_to_tags, cookbooks_to_tools, plan_rules_to_categories and plan_rules_to_tags. An earlier migration folded those filters into each cookbook's and rule's query_filter_string, which is what everything reads now, but it never emptied the join tables. The leftover rows are dead data that still references categories, tags and tools, and they still show up as the categories/tags/tools relationships of the models.

Expected:
- A migration that empties exactly those five tables and nothing else. The tables themselves stay (they are still mapped). plan_rules_to_households and recipes_to_categories are untouched.
- A unit test runs the migration's upgrade() through alembic's Operations context on a bare sqlite database that holds only those seven tables (two CHAR(32) columns each, three rows each, no other table), so the migration must use plain SQL against those five tables only, not the ORM or any other table. Afterwards the five legacy tables exist and hold 0 rows and the two unrelated ones still hold 3. Its downgrade() must then run without error on that same database, after which the legacy tables are still empty.
- After restoring each fixture backup (the backup restore test), every cookbook has no categories, tags or tools and every meal plan rule has no categories or tags; a cookbook or rule that had join rows in the backup has a non-empty query_filter_string; and a rule's households part ("household_id IN [...]") is still in its query_filter_string, since plan_rules_to_households is left alone.

bf16ca15.text:
Feature: subscribe to the household meal plan as an iCal calendar feed.

Users want their meal plan in their calendar app. Each household gets a secret feed token; the feed is public (the token is the only access control), so the token must never leak through the normal household endpoints. Frontend not graded.

Expected:
1. household_preferences gets mealplan_ical_token (String, nullable, unique, indexed), not filterable and not exposed: GET /api/households/self and GET /api/households/preferences never contain it, and PUT /api/households/preferences (say firstDayOfWeek 1) leaves it intact.
2. Token management under /api/households/mealplans/ical (registered before the mealplans router), response {householdId, mealplanIcalToken}: GET returns the token or null (null by default); POST generates a new url-safe token, replacing any old one (old feed URLs then 404), and returns it; DELETE sets it to null. POST and DELETE require can_manage_household (403); GET works for any household member.
3. The feed: GET /api/households/mealplans/ical/{token}, no authentication; 404 (detail "Calendar not found") for an unknown or cleared token; otherwise 200, content-type text/calendar, Content-Disposition inline; filename="mealplan.ics", Cache-Control no-cache. The body starts "BEGIN:VCALENDAR\r\n" and ends "END:VCALENDAR\r\n"; lines are CRLF-separated and folded to at most 75 bytes (continuations start with a space; multibyte characters never split); VERSION:2.0, PRODID, CALSCALE, METHOD:PUBLISH, X-WR-CALNAME "Mealie - {household name}". One VEVENT per entry of this household only, in date order, for the last FEED_HISTORY_DAYS (90) days (exactly 90 days old is kept, 91 dropped) and all future dates. Event: UID "mealplan-{entry id}-{group id}@mealie", DTSTAMP, SUMMARY "{Type}: {recipe name or title}" with the type translated and capitalized ("Dinner"), DESCRIPTION from the entry text and recipe URL, URL "{BASE_URL}/g/{group slug}/r/{recipe slug}" for a recipe entry, TRANSP:TRANSPARENT. Text is escaped: backslash, ";" and "," get a backslash, line breaks become "\n" ("Leftovers, again; sorry" -> "Leftovers\, again\; sorry"). Without a time the event is all-day: DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD, DTEND;VALUE=DATE the next day.
4. Query parameters (camelCase): types (entry types; unknown such as "brunch" -> 422) keeps only those; includeNotes=false drops entries without a recipe; tz (IANA name, unknown -> 422, default the server zone) plus a time per type (breakfast, lunch, dinner, side, snack, drink, dessert; e.g. dinner=18:30) makes that type a one-hour event in UTC: dinner 18:30 Europe/Berlin on a July day gives DTSTART {date}T163000Z, DTEND {date}T173000Z; types without a time stay all-day.
5. Helpers in mealie.services.household_services.mealplan_ical_service: _escape_text(value) ("a\\b;c,d\r\ne\nf" -> "a\\\\b\\;c\\,d\\ne\\nf") and _fold(line) (a short line unchanged; a 212-character line folds into "\r\n "-joined parts of at most 75 bytes that unfold to the line; 40 repetitions of a pasta emoji and an umlaut fold without splitting a character).

cd2097ee.text:
Feature: in-app customization of the AI prompts, per group, replacing the OPENAI_CUSTOM_PROMPT_DIR setting.

Today a custom prompt is a file under OPENAI_CUSTOM_PROMPT_DIR, global to the instance. Groups should append to or override each prompt in the app (frontend not graded); the setting goes away, migrated into the database.

Expected:
1. New table ai_prompt_overrides: id (GUID, primary key), settings_id (GUID, foreign key to ai_provider_settings.id, not null, indexed), name (String, not null, indexed; dot notation such as "recipes.build-recipe"), mode (String, not null: "append" or "override"), content (String, not null), base_prompt_hash (String, nullable), the base timestamps, unique (name, settings_id). AIProviderSettings gets a prompt_overrides relationship (delete-orphan). A group-scoped repository repos.group_ai_prompt_overrides (create fills in settings_id) and schemas AIPromptMode, AIPromptOverrideCreate/Update/Save/Out, AIPromptOut, AIPromptsOut in mealie.schema.group.ai_providers.
2. Prompt files: compile-source and transcribe-audio move to a "system" category (names system.compile-source, system.transcribe-audio); the debug prompt moves to OpenAIService.TESTING_DIR / "debug.txt", which ping() reads directly. OpenAIService.get_prompt_names() lists every built-in prompt, user prompts before system ones; get_default_prompt(name) returns the file content, OSError ("Unable to load prompt") when missing or empty; is_system_prompt(name); _hash_prompt(content) is the sha256 hex digest.
3. get_prompt: an "override" replaces the default, an "append" is added after it. The reserved name "global" (GLOBAL_PROMPT_NAME in mealie.services.openai.openai, append only) is group-wide instructions appended to every non-system prompt, before the prompt's own. Appended text follows the default (or override) as: blank line, "###", a sentence saying these instructions take priority over conflicting ones above, "---", blank line, the instructions joined by blank lines (so the result ends with "\nEXTRA" or "GLOBAL EXTRA\n\nPROMPT EXTRA"); data injections come after. Other prompts' overrides are ignored; system prompts get no global instructions; with repos.group_id None nothing is applied and repos.group_ai_prompt_overrides.get_all() is never called.
4. Routes: GET, PUT /{prompt_name}, DELETE /{prompt_name} under /api/groups/ai-providers/prompts (can_manage, else 403) and under /api/admin/groups/{group_id}/ai-providers/prompts (admins only). GET returns {globalInstructions: string or null, prompts: [{name, isSystem, defaultContent, mode or null, content or null, defaultChanged}]}, every built-in prompt. PUT {mode, content} (at most 20000 characters, blank -> 422) creates or replaces the group's customization and returns the same payload; unknown names ("recipes.does-not-exist", "debug", "..secrets") answer 404 on PUT and DELETE; "global" with mode override answers 400; the stored base_prompt_hash is the current default's hash, and defaultChanged is true only for an override whose stored hash differs from the current default. DELETE removes it (200 even when none). Customizations are per group.
5. The migration creates the table and imports the legacy files: OPENAI_CUSTOM_PROMPT_DIR leaves AppSettings and the migration reads it itself (environment, .env, secrets dir); for every row of ai_provider_settings it inserts "override" rows for recipes/build-recipe.txt, parse-recipe-ingredients, parse-recipe-video, resolve-organizers and translate-recipe (names recipes.*), recipes/compile-source.txt (system.compile-source) and general/transcribe-audio.txt (system.transcribe-audio), with the current built-in prompt's hash; blank files, removed prompts and general/debug.txt are skipped. A unit test runs upgrade() on a bare sqlite database holding only ai_provider_settings(id CHAR(32)), so the migration creates the table itself and reads the ids with plain SQL; without the variable it inserts nothing.

a1a49d22.text:
Feature: session token refresh, a server-set session cookie, remember-me that persists instead of extending, and password changes that evict other sessions.

Today the SPA writes the session cookie itself (Safari caps such cookies at seven days), remember-me widens the token lifetime (a no-op when TOKEN_TIME is longer), clients cannot know when to refresh, and changing a password leaves every existing session valid.

Expected:
1. mealie.core.security exposes ALGORITHM, ISS ("mealie") and create_access_token(data, expires_delta=None) returning (token, lifetime as timedelta); every token carries iss, iat and exp = iat + lifetime; the default lifetime is TOKEN_TIME hours. create_file_token still returns a string (with iss and iat). validate_file_token on a signed token without a "file" claim raises HTTPException 401 instead of crashing.
2. Login (POST /api/auth/token) answers {access_token, token_type "bearer", expires_in}: the lifetime in seconds (TOKEN_TIME * 3600), equal to exp - iat. remember_me no longer changes the lifetime; it is recorded as the boolean "rme" claim. The response sets the cookie mealie.access_token=<token> with Path=/, not HttpOnly, and a Max-Age (the lifetime) only when remember_me is true, a session cookie otherwise. The OIDC callback and native exchange do the same with OIDC_REMEMBER_ME.
3. session_cookie_attrs(request) in mealie.routes.auth.auth returns {path "/", secure, samesite, partitioned}: secure when the scheme is https or the first entry of X-Forwarded-Proto is https; samesite "none" and partitioned true only when secure and X-Mealie-Embedded: true is sent; otherwise "lax" and false.
4. Refresh becomes POST /api/auth/refresh: 401 without or with an invalid token; returns a new token with the same expires_in, keeps rme, re-sends the cookie (Max-Age when remembered), and the new token works for GET /api/users/self. A long-lived API token (long_token claim) cannot be refreshed: 400.
5. POST /api/auth/logout answers with Set-Cookie mealie.access_token= and Max-Age=0, same attributes.
6. get_auth_token(request, token) in mealie.core.dependencies.dependencies (async, on the soft-fail bearer scheme): the bearer token wins, else the mealie.access_token cookie, else ""; other cookies are ignored. get_current_user and try_get_current_user take the token from it.
7. users gets tokens_valid_after (naive UTC datetime, nullable, default None; on PrivateUser). User.update_password sets it to now floored to the second. get_current_user rejects (401) a session token whose iat is missing or earlier; API tokens are validated by their own path and exempt. So after PUT /api/users/password the old session gets 401 on /api/users/self, an API token created before the change still works, and a fresh login with the new password works.
8. DELETE /api/users/api-tokens/{id} is allowed to the owner only, by user id: another user of the same group gets 403 and the token survives for its owner to delete.
9. AlchemyExporter.look_for_datetime must list every NaiveDateTime column of the models (tokens_valid_after, and the existing completed_date which is missing today); a test derives the set from the metadata.

7808c944.text:
Feature: use the OIDC "picture" claim as the user's avatar.

Users who sign in through OIDC already have a profile picture at their identity provider; Mealie should pick it up on login. The claim can be user-edited at some providers, so the fetch must be vetted like any URL a user hands us, and it must never break a login.

Expected:
1. The users table gets external_avatar_hash (String, nullable, default None), exposed on PrivateUser: the sha256 hex digest of the picture URL the stored avatar was built from.
2. On every OIDC login (OpenIDProvider.authenticate, new or existing user), when the claims carry a string "picture": vet the URL, download it, convert it to webp as profile.webp in PrivateUser.get_directory(user_id), rotate the user's cache_key (cache.new_key()) and store the hash through repos.users.patch. When the stored hash already equals the claim's hash, no request is made. A missing, empty or non-string claim (123, a dict) makes no request. Any failure (connection error, undecodable image, a malformed URL such as "https://[::1" or a 300-character host label) leaves the login successful and the user's cache_key and hash untouched (hash None).
3. Vetting (_is_safe_picture_url): the host of OIDC_CONFIGURATION_URL is allowed over http or https even on a private address (a self-hosted provider on the LAN). Any other URL must be https (file:, ftp:, http: and "not-a-url" are refused without a request), and every address the host resolves to (socket.getaddrinfo, called through the provider module's socket so tests can pin it) must be a global address: 127.0.0.1, 10.0.0.5, 192.168.1.10, 169.254.169.254, ::1 and fd00::1 are refused, as is an unresolvable host. Nothing is requested before vetting.
4. Download (_fetch_picture): requests.get(url, timeout, stream=True, allow_redirects=False), called through the provider module's requests; redirects (301, 302, 303, 307, 308) are followed by hand, each Location resolved against the current URL (relative paths allowed) and vetted again before it is requested, so a hop to a private address or a downgrade to http stops the fetch without a second request; a redirect without a Location is an error; at most MAX_PICTURE_REDIRECTS (3) hops, i.e. four requests, then give up. _read_capped refuses a Content-Length above MAX_PICTURE_BYTES (5 MiB) and stops reading once the streamed body exceeds it. The downloaded temp file is moved into place (shutil.move), leaving nothing behind.

36d716a4.text:
Feature: structured recipe times.

Recipe times (total, prep, perform) are free text that cannot be summed, converted or exported as schema.org durations. Store seconds next to each text field whenever the source is a clear duration; keep the text otherwise.

Expected:
1. recipes gets total_time_seconds, prep_time_seconds and perform_time_seconds (Integer, nullable); the text columns stay (cook_time too, deprecated). RecipeSummary gets the three (JSON totalTimeSeconds etc.) as integers 0..2**31-1 or null; 2**31 and -1 are validation errors.
2. The migration adds the columns and converts existing text into seconds, clearing the text, only when the whole string is unambiguously a duration; anything else is untouched. Its helpers live in the migration module and are tested directly. load_unit_words(locales_dir) maps every case-folded unit word of every locale's "datetime" translations (keys day, hour, minute, second; values "singular|plural") to its unit, dropping a word that means different units in different locales and skipping unreadable files. build_component_pattern(unit_words). parse_seconds(value, unit_words, pattern) accepts ISO 8601 in any case ("PT15M" 900, "P1DT2H" 93600), bare numbers as minutes ("30" 1800, "1.5" 90), and amounts with unit words of any locale, largest unit first, each at most once ("1 hour 30 minutes" 5400, "1 Stunde 30 Minuten", "1時間30分", "1.5 hours" 5400); None for blank, extra words ("about 30 minutes", "1 hour and 30 minutes", "Overnight", "none"), units out of order or repeated, unknown abbreviations ("30 mins", "1 hr"), zero, non-whole seconds ("PT0.5S"), months or years ("P1M"), over 2**31-1 seconds, invalid ISO. is_empty_time(value) is true for "none" ignoring case and spaces (the scraper's zero time); such text is cleared without seconds. format_seconds(seconds) gives English text (93690 "1 day 2 hours 1 minute 30 seconds"), which the downgrade writes back for every time the upgrade moved before removing the columns.
3. Cleaner (mealie.services.scraper.cleaner): clean_duration(value) -> seconds or None: numbers are minutes (30 -> 1800), ISO in any case including weeks and fractional seconds rounded ("PT1M1.53S" -> 62), timedelta, {"minValue": ...}, lists (first value); None for booleans, free text, months/years, "PT", negative, zero, too large, infinite. clean() fills prep/perform/totalTimeSeconds from the text when the seconds are not set and clears that text; existing seconds win. clean_time returns None for empty, zero or negative durations ("PT", "PT0S", timedelta(0), -5) and keeps non-duration text, "P1M" and "-PT1H" as text; parse_duration returns a timedelta or None. Scraped schema.org ISO times end up as seconds with no text.
4. The migrator fixtures import as seconds with no text: nextcloud (5100, 900, 4200), tandoor (120, None, None), myrecipebox (6900, 5400, 1500), recipekeeper (None, 1800, 3600), cookn (None, None, None).
5. AI import: structured times are not sent to the translation step ("PT1H30M" absent from its request) and survive it: totalTimeSeconds 5400, totalTime null; free text ("overnight") is translated, prepTimeSeconds null.
6. SPA schema.org JSON: iso_duration(seconds) in mealie.routes.spa (None and 0 -> None, 3690 "PT1H1M30S", 93600 "PT26H"); totalTime, cookTime (from perform) and prepTime come from the seconds, null without them; text is never emitted.

4a280cbd.text:
Feature: reverse proxy authentication.

Deployments behind an authenticating proxy (Authelia, Authentik and the like) want Mealie to trust the username the proxy forwards in a header instead of asking for a password. Login page wiring is not graded.

Expected:
1. AuthMethod (mealie.db.models.users.users) gets REVERSE_PROXY = "ReverseProxy". On PostgreSQL users.auth_method is a native enum type, so a migration must add the value there; on SQLite the column needs no change.
2. Settings: REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_ENABLED (default false), REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_HEADER ("X-Forwarded-User"), REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_SIGNUP_ENABLED (false), REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_SECRET (None) and REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_SECRET_HEADER ("X-Mealie-Reverse-Proxy-Secret"); a REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_READY property, true when enabled and a header name is set. AppInfo gains enable_reverse_proxy_auth and CheckAppConfig reverse_proxy_auth_ready and reverse_proxy_auth_disabled.
3. ReverseProxyProvider(session, username) in mealie.core.security.providers.reverse_proxy_provider, an AuthProvider whose authenticate() returns None for an empty username; finds the user by username or by email and returns the access token tuple; for an unknown username it creates the user (username and full_name = the username, email = the username when it contains "@", else "{username}@reverse-proxy.local", auth_method REVERSE_PROXY, not admin) when REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_SIGNUP_ENABLED is true (the created user is findable by username, any case), and returns None otherwise. Settings are read through get_app_settings() at call time (tests set environment variables and clear its cache).
4. GET /api/auth/reverse-proxy: 404 when the feature is not READY; when REVERSE_PROXY_AUTH_SECRET is set, the secret header must match it (constant-time comparison), else 401 (missing or wrong); a missing username header is 401; an unknown user with signup disabled is 401; otherwise 200 with {access_token, token_type, expires_in} and the session cookie set as a remembered login, and the token works for GET /api/users/self. The route reads the module-level settings object of mealie.routes.auth.auth (tests patch READY, the header name, the secret and the signup flag on it).

30ba9a65.text:
Fix: recipes show no image, or request an image that is not there; keep recipes.image in sync with the files on disk.

recipes.image is a cache key, and the frontend now reads its presence as "this recipe has a picture". Rows have drifted from the disk: a recipe with an image file but no key shows the placeholder, and a recipe with a key but no file asks the media route for a 404 on every render. Three causes: the scraper stamps a key even when the image download failed, importers do the same, and a PUT that omits the image field clears it (the update is a full overwrite) while the file stays.

Expected:
1. A key is stamped only when a file landed. finalize_scraped_recipe sets recipe.image to a new key only when RecipeDataService.scrape_image returned a path, and to None when the download returned nothing, when the scraped value is the "no image" placeholder, or when there is no URL. RecipeDataService.scrape_image returns the written path or None; the migration helpers import_image and scrape_image return the path or None; the migrators persist each recipe with image None and record a key (repos.recipes.update_image, which now returns a string key from cache.new_key()) only after a file was written. PUT /api/recipes/{slug}/image/url answers 400 "Image could not be downloaded" when nothing was written.
2. PUT /api/recipes/{slug} without an "image" key in the body keeps the stored key (and /api/media/recipes/{id}/images/original.webp keeps serving); a body with "image": null still clears it.
3. A data migration reconciles the existing rows once. A recipe has an image on disk when {RECIPE_DATA_DIR}/{dashed uuid}/images/original.webp is a file; the migration module's _image_on_disk(recipe_data_dir, recipe_id) must find it whether the id arrives as a UUID, a dashed string or the undashed 32-character hex SQLite stores, and is false when the file is missing. Rows with a file but no key (or the legacy "no image" value) get a new key; rows with a key but no file are cleared, except when some rows claim an image and no recipe at all has a file (an unmounted volume), in which case the clearing half is skipped with a warning and only keys are restored.

Feature: a recipe scale on meal plan entries.

A meal plan entry points at a recipe but cannot say how much of it is planned (double batch, half batch). Store a scale factor per entry so the plan view and the shopping list quick add can use it (frontend not graded).

Expected:
- The group_meal_plans table gets recipe_scale: Float, not null, ORM default 1.0 and a server default of 1, so existing rows and rows inserted by code that does not know the column get 1.0. CreatePlanEntry (and so the update and read schemas) gets recipe_scale: float = 1.0, which must be greater than 0; JSON recipeScale.
- POST /api/households/mealplans without recipeScale stores 1: the create response, GET /api/households/mealplans/{id} and repos.meals.get_one(id).recipe_scale all report 1. With recipeScale 2.5 the create response and GET report 2.5. PUT /api/households/mealplans/{id} can change it (0.5), GET reflects it, and the date-range listing (GET /api/households/mealplans with page, perPage, start_date and end_date) includes recipeScale on each item. recipeScale 0 or -1 on POST or on PUT answers 422 and leaves the stored value as it was.
- The migration is additive. A unit test runs its upgrade() through alembic's Operations context on a bare sqlite table group_meal_plans(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, title VARCHAR NOT NULL) holding one row: afterwards the column exists, that row has recipe_scale 1.0, and a row inserted afterwards without the column also gets 1.0; downgrade() then removes the column and keeps both rows.
